name: (b) costs and token counts are estimates — Memory across sessions
pattern: Costs and token counts are estimates \(~\)
asks: The cost and token figures Maestro records are estimates, not measured usage. They are the ~tokens and ~cost on the command-log lines, and the extension, the log's one writer (participant.ts:317), computes both where it builds each line (participant.ts:311-314): token counts by the character heuristic, text length divided by 3.7 (token-estimator.ts:22), and the cost as those counts priced at the fixed default table rate, because no model is passed (cost-estimator.ts:39, :66). A run that writes no line records no figure.

name: (c) /teach-maestro asks the coding agent to interview and save .maestro.md — First run
pattern: asks your coding agent to interview you about the project and save the answers as `\.maestro\.md` in its root
asks: On every route, /teach-maestro hands the coding agent the skill text that tells it to interview the reader about the project and save the answers as .maestro.md in the project root: on the skill-file route the agent loads source/skills/teach-maestro/SKILL.md, which says both; on the MCP route the server serves that same text as the teach-maestro prompt; on the extension route VS Code's palette, sidebar and chat send @maestro /teach-maestro, whose participant passes the text to the model, while Cursor and Antigravity send /teach-maestro to their own agent, beside the SKILL.md the extension synced into the skills folders.
